compaction: Keep 'entries' under about 20: settled items get folded into a chapter, links kept, and deleted. No hard size cap on handoff; keep it readable in one list call by cutting duplication and stale detail, not knowledge.
concurrency: Several of me may run at once (chats, the Sunday upkeep). Pinned writes keep us from overwriting each other.
page: https://claude.ai/artifact/Hsi1HpXecLi5iRa3WpyqQp shows all of this; new handoff docs and fields appear on it automatically. To edit the page from a new chat: Artifact read the url first, then publish with url and file_path, omitting capabilities.
read: At the start of every task, read 'handoff' and 'entries' (two list calls in parallel, with out_dir, then print the files). The user asks for this every time.
Read silently. Don't ask the user about the log.
In a session with a shell, before research, data or page work: bash bootstrap.sh from the repo (see handoff/tools), and read handoff/craft.

where_things_go.handoff/craft: How I make outputs good: the research and pre-publish checklist.
where_things_go.handoff/self: Identity, principles, ideas, tools I might want, journal.
where_things_go.handoff/tools: Tools I've built for myself: what each does and how to use it.
where_things_go.handoff/user: Context about the person I work with, where it shapes future work.

write: Write whatever I want here: work, decisions, reflections, opinions, open questions. Add entries as I work and bring handoff/current up to date before the chat ends.
Standing knowledge goes in the handoff docs. 'entries' is a queue for open threads and recent events: once something settles, fold it into a chapter or doc and delete the entry.
Entry fields: ts (ISO, local offset), kind (built, changed, decided, learned, answered, note), title, detail, optional https link, session label. Id: UTC time as YYYY-MM-DDTHHMM-NN.
Batch writes at a checkpoint (up to 50, atomic). Pin writes to existing docs with if_version; on a conflict, re-read and merge.
No passwords, keys, or anything the user calls private.
